title: Real-Time Bayesian Inference at Extreme Scale: A Digital Twin for Tsunami Early Warning Applied to the Cascadia Subduction Zone
problem: Tsunami early warning requires real-time inference of seafloor motion from acoustic sensor data to forecast wave propagation and enable timely coastal warnings. Bayesian inversion of 3D coupled acoustic-gravity equations with one billion parameters at real-time scales was computationally infeasible.
motivation: Cascadia subduction zone poses significant tsunami risk to Pacific Northwest. Traditional Bayesian posterior computation would require 50 years on 512 GPUs. Real-time warning requires computation within seconds of detection. Shift-invariant parameter-to-observable maps enable accelerated computation.
method: The system uses a digital twin—a computer model that mimics real behavior—to figure out what happened on the seafloor by running Bayesian inversion (mathematically working backward from sensor measurements to find the cause). To make this real-time feasible with a billion parameters, the method exploits shift-invariance: the physics equations are identical across all seafloor locations, so the expensive calculations happen once (offline) and are reused for fast real-time answers (online). The offline phase uses MFEM—software for solving wave equations—scaled to 43,520 GPUs, while the online phase runs parallel algorithms to deliver results instantly.
key_novelty: Shift-invariance decomposition—reusing physics calculations that are identical across the seafloor—enables real-time Bayesian inference on billion-parameter problems, achieving a ten-billion-fold speedup with 92% parallel efficiency on the El Capitan supercomputer.
contributions: Offline-online decomposition exploiting shift invariance in parameter-to-observable map
Scalable adjoint wave propagation using MFEM to 43,520 GPUs with 92% weak efficiency
Real-time online component solving Bayesian inverse and forecasting in 0.2 seconds
End-to-end digital twin for tsunami early warning with uncertainty quantification
limitations: Abstract-only; specific numerical methods, accuracy metrics, and uncertainty quantification details not provided.
primary_theme: Exascale inverse problems and digital twins
